body:
## Problem

The optional between-waves re-gate (`gates.run_integration`, `template/src/pdca_harness/flow.py:1925` on branch `fix/593-stack-mode-append-only-fold-real-base-prs`) runs in the integration worktree, and nothing cleans that tree afterwards. Since #593 the next fold continues in the same worktree: `checkout -B <line> <tip>` (`integrate.py:362`), then `git merge` of each published branch. Build output the re-gate left behind (an untracked file in the way) makes `git merge` refuse, and the run stops.

The round-3 code review found it. Round 4 fixed the message (a merge failure with no conflicting path is now reported as a git-step failure, not an overlap, `integrate.py:399-407`), but not the cause: the run still stops on leftover build output with `regate_between_waves` on. The `merge --abort` return code is also ignored.

## Done when

The fold resets and cleans the integration worktree (`git reset --hard` + `git clean -fdx`, or equivalent) before `checkout -B`, or the re-gate runs in a separate tree. A test runs a re-gate that writes an untracked file, then a continuing fold, and the fold succeeds.

Found by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-02 (issue_593 iteration-v3 code review).
title: stack mode: the between-waves re-gate leaves build output in the integration worktree, so the next fold's merge can refuse and stop the run
